text:
<edits>
component: harness.py (answer post-processing)
candidates: inv1, dom1, agg1
change: Added string replacement to strip markdown characters ("**", "*", "__", "_") from the extracted answer before returning it. Refactored to assign answer to a variable before returning, rather than returning directly from the ternary expression.
observed: base1 rollout produced `**Saturday**` (with markdown formatting). All three candidate rollouts (inv1, dom1, agg1) produced `Saturday` (plain text). The task specification "Answer with the weekday name" names a textual value; the LLM naturally wrapped it in markdown in all cases. The candidates' post-processing step removed the formatting, yielding a plain weekday name that aligns better with the implicit task requirement.
verdict: helped
</edits>

<experience>
cue: A task specifies that the answer should be a particular named textual value (weekday, month name, color, etc.), and the LLM semantically produces the correct value but naturally wraps it in markdown formatting.

lesson: In the harness.py solve function, after extracting the answer text from the LLM reply, apply post-processing via `.replace()` to strip markdown formatting characters ("**", "*", "__", "_") before returning the answer.

evidence: base1 (no stripping) delivered `**Saturday**`. All three candidates—inv1, dom1, agg1—applied identical markdown stripping and delivered `Saturday`. The task asks for "the weekday name" (plain text), not formatted output. Each candidate's rollout trajectory shows the LLM producing `**Saturday**` and the post-processing step removing the delimiters. Library entry ood-dates-005 independently documents this exact pattern (named-value task → markdown wrapping → mechanical code-based stripping) as a validated, transferable lesson in the dates domain.

confidence: high. The execution contrast is clear and reproducible across all three implementations. The semantic correctness is unchanged; only the format divergence from task spec is addressed. The library provides independent validation that this pattern transfers. All candidates succeeded with the same edit, eliminating confounding.
</experience>
